newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended slightly up in slow trading on Thursday due to retail investors buying, traders said.
The most active April 1997 contract ended at 20,780 yuan ($2,504) per tonne, rising 140 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 20,750 and hit a high of 20,820.
January rose 20 to 20,320, February 90 to 20,450, March 110 to 20,610, May 150 to 20,800 and June 190 to 20,790.
Combined volume fell to 17,220 tonnes from 22,770.
Copper opened higher and rose further for most of the session.
Traders said many investors were staying on the sidelines today following the New Year holiday and some retail investors pushed the copper up.

"Investors remained in a holiday mood," one trader said. "Most of them do not want to build positions at the moment, but some retail investors pushed the prices up on expectations of an upward trend early this year."
Traders expect copper to move between 20,500 and 21,000 yuan in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down. The only traded January contract fell 130 to end at 13,820 yuan per tonne after 150 tonnes traded.
